title: Fix 'zsh: command not found: pip' on macOS
summary: The error means the terminal cannot find a program named pip. You can run pip through python3 instead, which works even when the plain pip name is not on PATH.

aliases.text: pip is not recognized mac terminal
how to run pip on mac terminal
pip not working in mac terminal
команда pip не найдена на маке
pip не работает в терминале mac
как запустить pip на маке через python3

prerequisites: Python 3 is installed on the Mac, for example from python.org or Homebrew

steps.explain: Check whether a plain pip command exists on your PATH. If this prints nothing, the pip name is missing, which is why zsh reports command not found.
steps.expect: Usually no output when only pip3 is installed. If pip exists, a path such as /opt/homebrew/bin/pip is printed.

steps.explain: Run pip as a module through python3. This uses the same Python that python3 points to, so it does not need the pip name on PATH.
steps.expect: A line starting with 'pip', a version number, and the path of the Python it belongs to.

steps.explain: Install a Python package with pip through python3. Replace <PACKAGE> with the package name. If pip reports 'externally-managed-environment', this Python does not allow global installs, so use a virtual environment instead.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the Python package to install

verify.expect: A line starting with 'pip' followed by a version number.

source.title: python3 manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
